sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Radhey Krishna Shukla,Santosh Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Deepak Verma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The instant bail application has been filed with a prayer to release the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 99 of 2021, registered under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468 I.P.C., Police Station Gagha,
District Gorakhpur during pendency of the trial.
Allegation in the FIR is that applicant, who runs a Grahak Sewa Kendra in District Gorakhpur, has induced the informant that on fixed deposit he would get benefit of 8.50% interest.
Informant deposited Rs.1,50,000/- but on maturity he found that accused persons fled away from he Grahak Sewa Kendra and locked the office.

Yogendra vs State Of U.P. on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52062034/
1
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.

Co-accused, Sanjay, who is nephew of the applicant, has been granted bail by co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 15.03.2023 on condition that he would deposit Rs.1,50,000/- by way of electronic mode in bank account of the informant.

Sunny, brother of co-accused, Sanjay, had deposited the whole amount of Rs.1,50,000/-
in the account of informant by electric mode, a copy of payment has been annexed as annexure 6 to the affidavit and the applicant's case is identical to the co-accused, hence, the applicant is also entitled to be enlarged on bail on the ground of same footing.
Criminal history of the applicant has been explained in para 12 to the affidavit.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 11.11.2022.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and co-operate in trial.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail prayer of the applicant.

Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of offence, evidence, complicity of accused and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and the law laid down by the Apex Court in Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. C.B.I. & Another, S.L.P.(Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. C.B.I. & Another, S.L.P.(Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant, Yogendra, who is involved in the aforesaid case crime, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/ pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.

2. The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
3. The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Order Date :- 19.5.2023
